items.headline: A quantum prediction from 1931 just came to life
items.teaser: Nearly a century after physicist Hans Bethe predicted them, scientists have created and directly observed unusual quantum states known as…
items.story:
Nearly a century after physicist Hans Bethe predicted them, scientists have created and directly observed unusual quantum states known as “Bethe strings” in an ultracold gas. By cooling cesium atoms to near absolute zero and trapping them in thousands of tiny one-dimensional tubes, researchers were able to make groups of atoms bind together without ordinary chemical bonds. These strange clusters could contain six or more particles and even collide with one another without falling apart.

items.story: ന്യൂനപക്ഷ മണ്ഡലത്തിൽ ബിജെപിക്ക് ഭൂരിപക്ഷം 75816; ബംഗാൾ രാഷ്ട്രീയത്തിൽ വരുന്നത് വൻ മാറ്റമെന്ന് സൂചന News18 Malayalamബംഗാളിലെ നന്ദിഗ്രാമിൽ ബിജെപിക്ക് വിജയം, തമിഴ്നാട്ടിൽ ടിവികെ ആധിപത്യം, 2000 വോട്ട് നേടാതെ ഇടതുപക്ഷം Manorama Onlineഉപതിരഞ്ഞെടുപ്പ് വോട്ടെണ്ണല്‍; തമിഴ്‌നാട്ടില്‍ ടിവികെ ആധിപത്യം; പുതുച്ചേരിയിലും ബംഗാളിലും അസമിലും എന്‍ഡിഎ Mathrubhumiഒട്ടും 'മമത'യില്ലാതെ ബംഗാള്‍; നന്ദിഗ്രാമിലും രജിനഗറിലും ബിജെപിക്ക് തകര്‍പ്പന്‍ ജയം Samakalika Malayalamദ്രാവിഡ കോട്ടകളിൽ വിള്ളൽ വീഴ്ത്തി തമിഴക വെട്രി കഴകം;

Media Oneഗ്യാനേഷ് കുമാറിനെതിരെ കേരളത്തില്‍ രണ്ടാമത്തെ അഴിമതിക്കേസും തലപൊക്കുന്നു Siraj Daily

items.headline: Nightjar wings reveal a trade-off between hunting slowly and traveling far
items.teaser: The European nightjar (Caprimulgus europaeus) is a nocturnal migratory bird that travels between Europe and southern Africa each year. Ho…
items.story: The European nightjar (Caprimulgus europaeus) is a nocturnal migratory bird that travels between Europe and southern Africa each year. However, its wings are not only used for long-distance journeys. When hunting insects, the nightjar must be able to slow down, turn sharply and fly at low speeds. Researchers at Lund University have now shown how this trade-off is reflected in the bird's flight mechanics. The study is published in the journal PLOS Biology.

items.headline: A quantum prediction from 1931 just came to life
items.teaser: Nearly a century after physicist Hans Bethe predicted them, scientists have created and directly observed unusual quantum states known as…
items.story: Nearly a century after physicist Hans Bethe predicted them, scientists have created and directly observed unusual quantum states known as “Bethe strings” in an ultracold gas. By cooling cesium atoms to near absolute zero and trapping them in thousands of tiny one-dimensional tubes, researchers were able to make groups of atoms bind together without ordinary chemical bonds. These strange clusters could contain six or more particles and even collide with one another without falling apart.
